introduction: The most important job of the RBI is formulating the 'Monetary Policy'. At this level, we will understand what this policy aims to achieve, how it balances inflation and growth, and the committee responsible for making these massive decisions.

core_concepts.title: What is Monetary Policy?
core_concepts.description: Monetary Policy is the process by which the RBI controls the 'Supply of Money' and 'Interest Rates' in the economy. The ultimate goal is to maintain price stability (control inflation) while keeping in mind the objective of economic growth.

core_concepts.title: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)
core_concepts.description: Formed in 2016 (based on the Urjit Patel Committee's recommendations), the MPC is a '6-member' statutory body tasked with setting the benchmark interest rate (Repo Rate). It consists of 3 members from the RBI (including the Governor, who acts as the ex-officio chairperson) and 3 external members appointed by the Government of India.

core_concepts.title: Inflation Targeting Framework
core_concepts.description: Under an agreement with the government, the RBI is legally bound to keep India's retail inflation (measured by CPI) at a target of '4%', with a comfortable tolerance band of +/- 2% (meaning inflation should ideally stay between 2% and 6%).

core_concepts.title: Expansionary vs. Contractionary Policy
core_concepts.description: 1. Expansionary (Dovish): RBI lowers interest rates -> Loans become cheaper -> People borrow and spend more -> Money supply increases -> Growth is boosted (but inflation may rise). 2. Contractionary (Hawkish): RBI raises interest rates -> Loans become expensive -> Spending drops -> Money supply decreases -> Inflation is controlled.

important_entities.name: The Casting Vote
important_entities.significance: In the 6-member Monetary Policy Committee, decisions are taken by a majority vote. If there is a tie (3 vs 3), the RBI Governor does not have a veto, but he/she does have a 'Casting Vote' to break the tie.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: While the Government of India appoints 3 out of the 6 members to the MPC, the government 'cannot' directly order the RBI to print more money or set a specific interest rate. The MPC operates with institutional autonomy.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Always remember the RBI's legal mandate for inflation: Target is 4%, Lower limit is 2%, Upper limit is 6%.

exam_strategy_tips: Assertion/Reasoning questions frequently ask about the composition of the MPC. Remember it is an evenly split committee: 3 from RBI, 3 from the Government.
